summary.suggested: In a letter to the St. Louis Evening Dispatch, Tom Allen answered a Republican writer who said he could not stand a long fight, listing his long English battles with Posh Price, George Iles, Bob Smith and Joe Goss.

metadata.notes: Masthead: 'The Dispatch: St. Louis, Tuesday Evening, March 23, 1875'. Before the Post-Dispatch (1878-12). Current summary is over 300 characters.

facts.fact: Allen wrote that he stood unrivaled as middleweight champion of England, had fought nineteen battles in the ring, and had fought for more money than any man living
facts.quote: I have fought nineteen battles in the ring, and I have fought for more money than any man living.

facts.fact: Allen wrote that his fights in England with Posh Price and George Iles lasted two hours five minutes and two hours, and his fight with Bob Smith three hours
Allen wrote that his last fight with Joe Goss in England lasted one hour fifty-seven minutes until darkness, and the next morning doctors advised them to agree to a draw
Allen wrote that Gallagher, Davis and McCoole did not last above twenty minutes against him, answering the Republican's claim that he could not stand a long fight
facts.quote: Now these men did not last above twenty minutes when they met me, and I suppose that is why I cannot stand a long fight.

facts.fact: Allen wrote that Rocky Moore was the first man he sparred with in America, and that the crowd tried to mob him and stopped the sparring because he hit Moore so hard
facts.quote: he was the first man I sparred with in the country, and I made a child of him with the gloves
